places.name: The Dalí Museum
places.hours_text: Daily 10am–6pm, Thursdays until 8pm. Closed Thanksgiving and Christmas Day.
places.price_text: Gallery admission: adults (18–64) $32; seniors 65+, educators, fire, police and military $29; students (13–17 and college) $22; youth 6–12 $12; 5 and under and members free. Dome show add-on $15. Thursdays after 5pm: adults and seniors $16, ages 6–17 and college $10.
places.summary: Museum devoted to Salvador Dalí, built on the collection of A. Reynolds and Eleanor Morse; the museum says it holds over 2,400 works in all media. Gallery admission covers the permanent collection, special exhibitions and the Avant-garden; the Dalí Dome shows immersive projections for an added fee.
places.quote: The Dalí Museum celebrates the life and work of Salvador Dalí (1904-1989) and features works from the artist’s entire career.
places.accessibility: Galleries and the Will Raymund Theater are accessible for manual and electric mobility devices; 9 accessible parking spaces next to the museum; courtesy wheelchairs at the information station, first come, first served.
places.parking_text: On-site lot $10 (cards only), first come, first served; city garages, surface lots and street parking nearby.

places.name: Museum of Fine Arts, St. Petersburg
places.hours_text: Tuesday–Sunday 10am–5pm; Art After Dark on Thursdays 5–8pm; closed Monday, Thanksgiving and Christmas Day.
places.price_text: Adults $16; seniors 65+, military, Florida educators and college students $14; youth 7–17 $10; 6 and under and Museums for All (SNAP EBT) free. Art After Dark $16 for non-members, youth 17 and under free.
places.summary: Art museum on the downtown waterfront, founded by collector Margaret Acheson Stuart and opened in 1965; the museum says it was the city's first art museum. The collection galleries are closed Sep 22–Nov 21, 2026 for a reinstallation; the New African Masquerades exhibition, shop and café stay open.
places.quote: The MFA opened to the public in 1965–the first art museum in the city.
places.status_note: Collection galleries close Sep 22, 2026 and re-open Nov 21, 2026 during the 'Reimagination'; the New African Masquerades exhibition, the MFA Shop, Café Clementine and programs continue (per mfastpete.org/about/reimagination, checked 2026-09-27).
places.parking_text: Paid self-parking in the south lot and along Bayshore Drive (Parkmobile or kiosk); garages and lots within walking distance.
places.notes: Verifier 2026-09-27: reimagination page says the collection galleries 'close September 22' (the researcher had Sep 21); fixed.

places.name: Chihuly Collection
places.hours_text: Monday–Saturday 10am–5pm, Sunday noon–5pm. Closed Thanksgiving and Christmas; closes at 3pm on some holidays.
places.price_text: Adults $22; seniors 65+ and military $20; students (6–18 or college ID) $16; Museums for All $3; 5 and under free.
places.summary: Permanent collection of glass art by Dale Chihuly, run by the Morean Arts Center in a building designed for it. A ticket includes a live glassblowing demonstration at the Morean Glass Studio nearby.
places.quote: This presentation is unique as it is the first installation of Chihuly art in a building designed specifically for that purpose.
places.parking_text: Street parking and the 4th floor of the Publix parking garage during business hours.

places.name: Morean Arts Center
places.hours_text: Monday–Saturday 10am–5pm; closed Sunday.
places.price_text: Gallery free.
places.summary: Contemporary art gallery and art school on Central Avenue with changing exhibitions and year-round classes. The same nonprofit runs the Chihuly Collection and the Morean Glass Studio nearby and the Morean Center for Clay in the Warehouse Arts District.
places.quote: The Morean Arts Center offers an amazing contemporary art gallery, FREE and open to the public daily PLUS affordable art classes year-round.
places.parking_text: Street parking and the 4th floor of the Publix parking garage during business hours.

places.name: Morean Glass Studio and Hot Shop
places.hours_text: Wednesday–Sunday noon–5pm. Live demonstrations Wednesday–Saturday at 12, 1, 2 and 3pm; Sunday at 1, 2 and 3pm.
places.price_text: Live glass demonstration $12, included with a Chihuly Collection ticket; personal glass experiences and classes priced separately.
places.summary: Glassblowing studio where resident artists work in front of visitors; the pieces are sold in the adjoining shop. You can also book a one-time hands-on glass experience or a class.
places.quote: Get behind the scenes and observe resident glass artists creating unique works of art.

places.name: Morean Center for Clay
places.hours_text: Wednesday–Saturday 10am–5pm; closed Sunday–Tuesday.
places.summary: Pottery center in a historic freight train depot in the Warehouse Arts District, home to more than 50 ceramic artists' studios, with classes and workshops. The Morean calls it the largest pottery studio in the Southeast.
places.quote: The largest pottery studio in the Southeast and one of the largest in the United States, the Morean Center for Clay is located in a historic freight train depot in the Warehouse Arts District of St. Petersburg.
places.parking_text: Free parking lot.

places.name: Imagine Museum
places.hours_text: Tuesday–Sunday 10am–5pm, Thursday until 8pm; closed Monday.
places.price_text: Adults $15; seniors 65+ and military $13; educators, college students and children 7–17 $10; 6 and under free.
places.summary: Museum of contemporary glass art from around the world, tracing the studio glass movement, with tours, scavenger hunts, a theater about glassmaking and a gift shop.
places.quote: Imagine Museum features a spectacular collection of contemporary glass art from around the world.
places.notes: The museum's own site (imaginemuseum.com) returned a SiteGround captcha to both curl and WebFetch on 2026-09-27, so the Visit St. Pete/Clearwater listing is the source; verifier should re-check hours and prices on imaginemuseum.com/plan-your-visit if reachable. Verifier 2026-09-27: imaginemuseum.com still returns a SiteGround captcha (curl and WebFetch); VSPC listing re-read and every field matched except 'members free', which is not on it (removed).

places.name: The James Museum of Western & Wildlife Art
places.hours_text: Daily 10am–5pm, Tuesdays until 8pm; last tickets 4:30pm (7:30pm Tuesday). Closed Thanksgiving and Christmas Day.
places.price_text: General admission $23; seniors 65+ $18; students, teachers and active military $15; youth 7–18 $10; 6 and under and members free. Tuesdays: adults $10, youth 7–18 $5.
places.summary: Museum of art of the American West and wildlife art: landscape paintings and sculpture, early Western art from 1900–1950, galleries of Native American art and contemporary Native jewelry (the Jewel Box), and a wildlife gallery.
places.quote: Showcasing sweeping landscape paintings and powerful sculptures that celebrate the land, people, and cultures of the American West.
places.parking_text: Levels 3 and 4 of the South Core Parking Garage behind the museum (enter at 101 1st Ave S), $2 per hour during regular operation.
places.notes: Verifier 2026-09-27: 'Most of the art is on the second level' was not on either page; removed.

places.name: Museum of the American Arts and Crafts Movement
aliases: Museum of the American Arts & Crafts Movement
places.hours_text: Tuesday–Saturday 10am–4pm, Sunday noon–4pm; closed to museum visitors Monday.
places.price_text: Adults $25; seniors 65+ $23; active military, students and educators $20; youth 6–17 $10; 5 and under free. Some seasonal exhibitions cost extra.
places.summary: Five-story museum founded by collector Rudy Ciccarello, devoted to the American Arts and Crafts movement (about 1890–1930): furniture, pottery, tiles, lighting, textiles and period rooms by Stickley, Frank Lloyd Wright, the Roycrofters, Grueby, Newcomb Pottery and others. It has a café, a store and a library.
places.quote: The Museum of the American Arts and Crafts Movement (MAACM) is the only museum in the world dedicated exclusively to the American Arts and Crafts movement.
places.status_note: The Fountain Garden is under construction for a gallery addition; follow signs for the temporary entrance (the 4th Street entrance is not wheelchair accessible), per the museum's visitor information page.
places.accessibility: Free wheelchairs at the admissions desk (a state ID is held as deposit); the 4th Street entrance is not wheelchair accessible during construction.
places.parking_text: MAACM Parking Garage next to the museum at 350 3rd Street North, $1 per hour; metered street parking nearby.

places.name: St. Petersburg Museum of History
places.hours_text: Monday–Saturday 10am–5pm, Sunday noon–5pm. Closed Thanksgiving, Christmas and Easter.
places.price_text: Adults $17; seniors 65+ $14; military and veterans $11; teachers, students and children 7–17 $9; 6 and under free.
places.summary: History museum at the entrance to the St. Pete Pier, with exhibits on the world's first commercial airline (including a replica of the Benoist airboat), 150 years of baseball in Schrader's Little Cooperstown and the history of tourism in the city. Perry's Porch restaurant is attached.
places.quote: Located at the entrance to the spectacular Pier District, the Museum of History has shared stories of the Sunshine City for a century.
places.parking_text: Metered St. Pete Pier Dolphin lot next to the museum, the Pelican lot, Pier street parking, or the Sundial garage (117 2nd Street N).

places.name: The Florida Holocaust Museum
places.hours_text: Daily 10am–5pm; last admission 4pm. Closed on the holidays listed on the museum's visitor guide (incl. Thanksgiving, Christmas Eve and Christmas Day).
places.price_text: General $25; seniors 65+, educators, students, active-duty military, law enforcement and veterans $18; 6 and under free; Museums for All free.
places.summary: Museum of the Holocaust in downtown St. Petersburg, begun in 1992 by businessman Walter P. Loebenberg and in its current building since 1998. It calls itself one of the largest Holocaust museums in the country.
places.quote: The Florida Holocaust Museum honors the memory of millions of innocent men, women and children who suffered or died in the Holocaust.
places.accessibility: ADA compliant and fully accessible; free wheelchairs at the admissions desk.
places.parking_text: Limited free parking at the museum; metered and on-street parking nearby. SunRunner stops at 5th Street South / 5th Street North.
places.notes: Verifier 2026-09-27: 'accessible parking on the north side along the alley' was not on the visitor guide as read; removed.

places.name: The Woodson African American Museum of Florida
aliases: Dr. Carter G. Woodson African American Museum
places.hours_text: Tuesday–Saturday noon–5pm.
places.price_text: Free admission.
places.summary: Museum of African American history in the former community center of Jordan Park, which the museum describes as St. Petersburg's first African American public housing community. Its Legacy Garden shows the sculpture 'Harriet Tubman: The Beacon of Hope'.
places.quote: The Woodson African American Museum of Florida’s current building was previously the community center and an administrative office for the Jordan Park community
places.status_note: Closed from Monday, Sep 21, 2026 for scheduled roof maintenance; regular hours resume Tuesday, Sep 29, 2026 (per woodsonmuseum.org, checked 2026-09-27).

places.name: Great Explorations Children's Museum
places.hours_text: Monday–Saturday 10:30am–4pm, Sunday noon–4pm. Closed Easter, July 4, Thanksgiving, Christmas Eve, Christmas Day and New Year's Day.
places.summary: Hands-on children's museum next to Sunken Gardens, with a preschool, camps and birthday parties.
places.quote: A place where kids can be creative, make discoveries and have fun!
places.notes: greatex.org returned a bot-check (HTTP 202, empty body) to curl and WebFetch on 2026-09-27; admission prices were not verified on a page we could read, so price_text is null.

places.name: Florida CraftArt
places.hours_text: Monday–Saturday 10am–5:30pm, Sunday noon–5pm; open until 8pm on Second Saturday (ArtWalk).
places.price_text: Free admission to the galleries.
places.summary: Statewide nonprofit for Florida fine craft, founded in 1951, with galleries of work by more than 200 Florida artists and an exhibition gallery, in the former Rutland's Department Store building on Central Avenue. It presents about ten exhibitions a year at no charge.
places.quote: Florida CraftArt presents ten exhibitions annually, at no charge to the public, ensuring barrier-free access to the arts for all.
places.notes: Verifier 2026-09-27: both the home page and About now say the galleries are open until 8 p.m. on Second Saturday; hours updated.

places.name: The St. Pete Pier
places.hours_text: Opens 30 minutes before sunrise, closes 11pm. Marketplace Friday–Sunday 10am–6pm (seasonal).
places.price_text: No charge to enter the Pier District; some special events are ticketed.
places.summary: Pier district on Tampa Bay with seven restaurants (Pier Teak has a rooftop level), public art, the Glazer Family Playground and a splash pad, Spa Beach, a fishing deck, a weekend marketplace and the Tampa Bay Watch Discovery Center. The St. Petersburg Museum of History sits at its entrance.
places.quote: There is no charge to enter the Pier District.
places.status_note: Janet Echelman's 'Bending Arc' sculpture is marked temporarily closed on the Pier's map (checked 2026-09-27).
places.accessibility: The Majeed Foundation Coastal Thicket boardwalk is ADA accessible.
places.parking_text: More than 500 paid spaces in the Dolphin and Pelican lots (6-hour maximum; first 4 hours $2/hour weekdays, $2.50/hour weekends); overflow at the Sundial garage and Al Lang lot; the free Downtown Looper and the SunRunner (5th Street N stop) serve the area.
places.notes: Verifier 2026-09-27: 'three ADA-compliant trams with four stops' is not on getting-here-parking, visit-pier or faq as read; removed. Rooftop confirmed on visit-pier ('Rooftop – Pier Teak').

places.name: Tampa Bay Watch Discovery Center
places.hours_text: Daily 10am–5pm; holiday exceptions listed on the site.
places.price_text: Adults and teens 13+ $8; seniors 60+ $6; military, Florida teachers and children 4–12 $3; 3 and under free.
places.summary: Small nature center on the St. Pete Pier's over-water walkway, run by the nonprofit Tampa Bay Watch, with interactive exhibits on the Tampa Bay estuary, live animals, a touch tank, daily programs and wildlife boat tours.
places.quote: Our exhibit gallery features interactive displays, live animals, and a touch tank for hands-on learning.
places.parking_text: Pier Pelican lot (paid), first come, first served; Pier trams stop at the center.

places.name: Grand Central District
places.summary: Main Street district along Central Avenue from 16th to 31st Street, just west of downtown, with more than 350 independent shops, restaurants, bars and galleries and many murals. The association calls it the birthplace of St. Pete's Pride Parade; it hosts Halloween on Central and a Christmas market.
places.quote: Founded in 2000 and located just west of downtown St. Petersburg, the Grand Central District is home to over 350 locally owned and operated independent businesses
places.notes: Point is the 2200 block of Central Avenue, mid-district (a representative point, not an address of the association).

places.name: Central Arts District
places.summary: Downtown stretch of Central Avenue from 3rd to 7th Street with murals, galleries and museums (Florida CraftArt, the Chihuly Collection, the Morean Arts Center), boutiques, restaurants, bars and music venues such as Jannus Live and the Floridian Social Club.
places.quote: runs along Central Avenue in downtown St. Pete, extending from 3rd Street to 7th Street (locals will refer to it as the 300 block to the 700 block)
places.notes: No district association site found; the Visit St. Pete/Clearwater district page is the source. Point is the 500 block of Central Avenue.

places.name: EDGE District
places.address: Central Avenue between 9th Street (MLK) and 16th Street
places.summary: Walkable Main Street district on Central Avenue between 9th Street (MLK) and 16th Street, with locally owned bars, restaurants and shops, between downtown and the Grand Central District.
places.quote: The EDGE District runs along St. Pete's Central Avenue between 9th Street (MLK) & 16th Street, and outward to both 1st Ave North & 1st Ave South.
places.notes: Point is the 1200 block of Central Avenue, mid-district.

places.name: Warehouse Arts District
places.summary: Former industrial area south of Central Avenue (between 16th and 31st streets, 1st Avenue North to 10th Avenue South) with artist studios, glass and clay studios, galleries, breweries and The Factory. The Warehouse Arts District Association's ArtsXchange campus holds studios and galleries and hosts the Second Saturday ArtWalk.
places.quote: The Warehouse Arts District features a collection of artist studios, galleries and events on the campus of ArtsXchange in St. Petersburg, FL.
places.notes: Boundaries from the Visit St. Pete/Clearwater district page. warehouseartsdistrictstpete.com is a hijacked domain (gambling spam) as of 2026-09-27: do not link it.

places.name: Beach Drive
places.summary: Downtown waterfront street along the bayfront parks, lined with restaurants with outdoor seating, bars and shops; it anchors what Visit St. Pete/Clearwater calls the Waterfront Museum District, between Beach Drive and 3rd Street from 7th Avenue South to 7th Avenue North, home to the Dalí, the MFA and other museums.
places.quote: You'll find St. Pete's Waterfront Museum District between Beach Drive and 3rd St., stretching from 7th Avenue South to 7th Avenue North.
places.notes: beachdrive.com is a commercial directory for the street, not an official body. Point is 300 Beach Dr NE.

places.name: The Deuces (22nd Street South)
places.summary: Corridor on 22nd Street South that was the center of St. Petersburg's Black business community during segregation, with hundreds of Black-owned businesses at its peak in the early 1960s. The Deuces Live Main Street program has worked on its revival since 2012; the Woodson African American Museum and murals are here.
places.quote: During segregation, 22nd Street South — lovingly known as “The Deuces” — became a hub of Black excellence, creativity, and commerce.
places.notes: Point is the Deuces Live office, 833 22nd Street South. history-region may also hold this corridor as a historic district; merge by id if so.

places.name: Duncan McClellan Gallery
places.hours_text: Monday–Saturday 11am–6pm, Sunday noon–4pm.
places.summary: Glass art gallery in the Warehouse Arts District with rotating shows of national and international glass artists, in a former fish and tomato packing plant with courtyards and sculpture gardens.
places.quote: The Duncan McClellan Gallery, located in St. Petersburg Florida, features rotating exhibitions showcasing national and internationally recognized glass artists.
places.notes: The home page lists two hours blocks (Mon–Sat 11–6 in one place, plus Sundays noon–4 in the footer).

places.name: FloridaRAMA
places.hours_text: Monday, Thursday and Friday noon–8pm; Saturday and Sunday 10am–8pm; closed Tuesday and Wednesday. Last entry 90 minutes before closing.
places.price_text: Ticketed; the art gallery is free.
places.summary: Indoor, ticketed immersive art installation about Florida stories, made by more than 80 mostly local artists, with a shop, a snack bar and a free art gallery. The entrance and ticket desk are inside Building 5 of The Factory St. Pete in the Warehouse Arts District, on the Pinellas Trail.
places.quote: Cooler than a museum, smarter than a theme park, and weirder than a carnival, FloridaRAMA is an immersive art experience located in St. Pete’s Warehouse Arts District.
places.accessibility: Wheelchair ramps, accessible restrooms, sensory bags and quiet areas; ADA-accessible parking on the Pinellas Trail side.
places.parking_text: Free parking in The Factory's north lot (Fairfield Ave S) and south lot (7th Ave S), plus street parking; on the Pinellas Trail with bike parking.
places.notes: Ticket prices are not printed on the pages read (sold through the ticketing link). thefactorystpete.com now redirects to floridarama.art; the site's news page cites 'Fairgrounds St. Pete expands and rebrands as FloridaRAMA', and the footer says it is operated by Fairgrounds Projects Inc. The Factory itself (a campus of studios and galleries) was not given its own record because its own site no longer describes it.

places.name: Zen Glass Studio & Gallery
places.hours_text: Tuesday–Saturday 10am–5pm, Sunday noon–5pm; Second Saturday 10am–9pm.
places.summary: Glass studio and gallery in the Warehouse Arts District, founded in 2002 by artists David Walker and Josh Poll, selling blown and sculpted glass and jewelry and teaching flameworking and glassblowing classes. Visitors can walk into the studio from the 6th Avenue South side.
places.quote: They feature a huge selection of blown and sculpted glass art, jewelry and sculpture in the gallery.
places.notes: Verifier 2026-09-27: Sunday noon–5pm is on zenglass.com/info (string-checked); added.

places.name: Saturday Morning Market
places.address: Al Lang Stadium parking lot, 1st Street South
places.hours_text: Saturdays 9am–2pm, October through May, at Al Lang Stadium; a smaller summer market runs 9am–1pm; no market in September.
places.price_text: Free admission.
places.summary: Weekly open-air market, running since 2002, with local farmers, ready-to-eat food, artisan food makers (baked goods, seafood, cheeses) and local artists and makers. The October–May season is held in the Al Lang Stadium lot downtown.
places.quote: Since 2002, the Saturday Morning Market has been a cornerstone of the St. Petersburg community, bringing together residents and visitors in a vibrant celebration of local food, art, music, and connection.
places.status_note: On its September break; returns to Al Lang Stadium on Saturday, Oct 3, 2026 for the October–May season (per ilovetheburg.com, Sep 1, 2026). The 2026 summer market (Jun 6–Aug 29) was held at St. Pete First United Methodist Church, 212 3rd Street North, because of construction at Williams Park (St. Petersburg Chamber event page).
places.parking_text: Nearby parking garages and city street parking.
places.notes: saturdaymorningmarket.com returned a bot-check (HTTP 202, empty) to curl and WebFetch on 2026-09-27; facts are from a dated local news article and the St. Petersburg Chamber's event page. Point is Al Lang Stadium (OSM).

places.name: Tyrone Square
places.summary: Simon shopping mall in west St. Petersburg with more than 55 stores (including Macy's, Dick's Sporting Goods and H&M) and more than 10 restaurants.
places.quote: St. Petersburg's Family-Favorite Shopping Destination. 55+ Stores. 10+ Restaurants.
places.notes: Weekly hours were not shown on the page as read (only the current day's hours), so hours_text is null.

places.name: Crislip Arcade
places.summary: Renovated 1926 open-air shopping arcade on the 600 block of Central Avenue: a covered walkway lined with small independent shops.
places.quote: a renovated 1926 shopping arcade located on the 600 block of Central Avenue, which is an open-air, covered hallway
places.status_note: Two arcade tenants, The Merchant and Crislip Cafe, were given notice to vacate 645 Central Ave in June 2026 (Patch, Jun 29, 2026), so the shops inside may have changed; the arcade itself was not reported closed.
places.notes: No official site found. Point is the OpenStreetMap feature for the arcade (tagged 645 Central Avenue); the source says only "600 block". Verifier 2026-09-27: quote shortened to the part WebFetch returned identically on re-read (the tail 'with a string of small retails shops' could not be confirmed verbatim).

places.name: St. Petersburg Shuffleboard Club
places.hours_text: Open play Tuesday and Thursday 6–9pm, Friday 7–10pm (Friday night St. Pete Shuffle), Sunday 9am–noon.
places.price_text: Open hours free for members, $10 per non-member; kids free.
places.summary: Shuffleboard club at Mirror Lake, organized in 1924 by six players as what the club calls the first strictly shuffleboard club in the world; the club says the game's rules were standardized here in the 1920s. Visitors can play during open hours, including Friday nights.
places.quote: So in 1924 a group of shuffleboard players — six in this case — organized what they called the Mirror Lake Park Shuffleboard Club, the first strictly shuffleboard club in the world
places.notes: history-region may also hold this as a historic site; merge by id.

places.name: Gulfport Waterfront District
places.summary: Small downtown on Boca Ciega Bay centered on Beach Boulevard, with independent galleries, boutiques, murals and more than a dozen restaurants, a beach, Williams Pier for fishing, the historic Casino ballroom (still used for swing dances), a twice-monthly Art Walk and the Gulfport Fresh Market.
places.quote: The twice-monthly Art Walk transforms Beach Boulevard into an open-air gallery.
places.notes: Source is the Gulfport Merchants Chamber (visitgulfportflorida.com). The City of Gulfport site (mygulfport.us) returned a bot-check on 2026-09-27. Point is the Gulfport Casino at the foot of Beach Blvd (OSM); the Casino ballroom itself belongs to venues-bay. Verifier 2026-09-27: 'below 28th Avenue South' and 'Shore Boulevard' are not on the source page; removed.

places.name: Gulfport History Museum
places.hours_text: Wednesday 10am–2pm, Thursday noon–4pm, Friday 10am–2pm, 1st and 3rd Saturdays noon–4pm.
places.price_text: Free.
places.summary: Small free museum of the history of Gulfport, which the listing calls one of Pinellas County's oldest incorporated cities.
places.quote: This museum documents the diversity and colorful history of one of Pinellas County's oldest incorporated cities.
places.notes: The city's museum page (mygulfport.us) returned a bot-check on 2026-09-27; facts are from the Visit St. Pete/Clearwater listing. gulfportmuseum.org is a different Gulfport (Mississippi). Verifier 2026-09-27: VSPC listing re-read: every field matched; its website link is mygulfport.us/gulfporthistorymuseumfl/ (url updated). A Jul 21, 2026 Gabber story shows the museum active.

places.name: Penny Lane Beatles Museum
places.hours_text: Wednesday–Sunday 10am–4pm.
places.price_text: General admission $15; children 8 and under free.
places.summary: Museum of Beatles memorabilia built from one collection, which moved in 2026 from a small upstairs space in Dunedin to the Palais Royale building downtown, one block off Central Avenue. The museum says it has more than 1,600 artifacts, nearly 1,000 on display at a time, and calls itself the only dedicated Beatles museum in the United States.
places.quote: The United States' only dedicated Beatles museum, now open in downtown St. Petersburg, Florida.
places.status_note: Reopened in downtown St. Petersburg in August 2026 after moving from Dunedin (the museum's news page lists 'A Massive Beatles Museum With 1,600 Rare Artifacts Just Opened In St. Pete', Aug 22, 2026). Admission is no longer free, per its visit page.
places.accessibility: Entrance by a ground-level ADA ramp; wheelchairs and standard strollers allowed in the galleries, though access may be limited in some areas; one ADA-compliant restroom.
places.parking_text: Metered street parking and public lots and garages within half a block; the Downtown Looper and trolley stop nearby.
places.notes: Verifier 2026-09-27: the museum's site (SiteGround captcha to curl and WebFetch) was read through the r.jina.ai reader. The VSPC listing the researcher used was out of date: it said 'Free admission' and Wed 10–4, Thu–Sun 11–3; the museum's visit page FAQ says 'General admission is $15 and children ages 8 and under are free. We are open Wednesday-Sunday 10-4pm.' (the same page still carries an 'Opening soon' block with these as 'Future Hours'; the home page says 'now open' and the press page lists an Aug 22, 2026 opening story). Re-check hours after launch.

places.name: John's Pass Village & Boardwalk
places.hours_text: Open daily; individual shop and restaurant hours vary.
places.summary: Waterfront boardwalk village at John's Pass with more than 100 merchants: shops, restaurants, the local fishing fleet, dolphin-watching and shelling tours, boat rentals, parasailing and jet skis. The beach is a short walk away.
places.quote: Over one hundred merchants inhabit the Village with unique retail shopping, a variety of restaurants, the local fishing fleet, dolphin watching and shelling tours, boat rentals, parasailing and jet skiing.
places.status_note: Businesses reopened in stages after Hurricanes Helene and Milton (2024); Hubbard's Marina reopened its main locations days after the storms and its boutique in September 2026 after structural repairs (Patch, Sep 10, 2026). A hotel for the village was approved in July 2026 (Tampa Bay Times, Jul 13, 2026).
places.parking_text: Pay-by-meter garage at the southwest corner and two pay-by-meter lots (Central lot and Beach lot).
places.notes: johnspass.com is the 'Discover John's Pass' merchant site (it calls the village 'Pinellas County’s #1 tourist attraction'). Phone and parking from the VSPC listing. Verifier 2026-09-27: The researcher's status_note attributed 'still recovering… lower deck not open' to Visit St. Pete/Clearwater; on re-read those words are visitor reviews on the VSPC listing, not the listing itself, so the note was rewritten from dated news. 'Pirate ship cruises' is not on johnspass.com as read; removed from the summary.

places.name: Pier 60
places.hours_text: Pier and bait house 7am–10pm; park 6am–9pm daily. Sunsets at Pier 60 runs year-round from 2 hours before to 2 hours after sunset, weather permitting.
places.summary: A 1,080-foot fishing pier with a bait house (bait, tackle, rentals, snacks), next to a beachfront park with a large beach playground, covered pavilions and telescopes. Sunsets at Pier 60, a free nightly festival of artisans and street performers held since 1995, takes place in the park.
places.quote: Sunsets at Pier 60 debuted on March 17, 1995 as a year-round nightly sunset celebration on the iconic Pier 60.
places.status_note: Closed for nearly a year after Hurricanes Helene and Milton (2024); the pier from the bait house to the T reopened Sep 1, 2025 while the city planned long-term repairs (FOX 13, Sep 1, 2025; Bay News 9, Sep 1, 2025). The city's beach page invites visitors to 'go fishing on Pier 60' (checked 2026-09-27).
places.notes: Fishing fees were not stated on the pages read. No closure notice was found on the city's beach page (which invites visitors to 'go fishing on Pier 60'); the verifier should confirm the pier's post-2024 status on myclearwater.com if a Pier 60 page exists. Animals are not permitted on Pier 60 or the bathing beaches (service dogs excepted), per sunsetsatpier60.com. Verifier 2026-09-27: Post-hurricane status confirmed from dated news (the researcher's open question 2).

places.name: Clearwater Marine Aquarium
places.hours_text: Daily 10am–5pm; last entry 30 minutes before closing. Closed Thanksgiving and Christmas; 9am–3pm Christmas Eve and New Year's Eve.
places.price_text: Adults (12+) $41.95; kids 3–11 $32.95; seniors 65+ $39.95; 2 and under free. Seasonal rates may apply.

heritage.story: The first Sunshine Skyway, a two-lane bridge, opened in 1954, and a second two-lane span opened in 1971. On May 9, 1980, the freighter Summit Venture struck a support pier during a squall; part of the southbound span collapsed and 35 people died. The present cable-stayed bridge, designed by Figg & Muller Engineering Group and built by the American Bridge Company, opened in 1987, and the old bridge was partly demolished and turned into two fishing piers.

# see-pinellas: attractions and points of interest in St. Petersburg, the Gulf beaches, Clearwater and North Pinellas

## What is covered
77 places (checked 2026-09-27): museums, galleries and studios, districts and main streets, piers and waterfronts, aquariums and animal attractions, weekly markets, notable shopping, family attractions and one landmark (the Sunshine Skyway Bridge).

- By region: St. Petersburg 37 (downtown-stpete 19, grand-central 9, south-stpete 3, gulfport 3, west-stpete 2, old-northeast 1); Clearwater & North Pinellas 28 (downtown-clearwater 7, tarpon-springs 7, dunedin 5, largo 4, safety-harbor 4, palm-harbor 1); Gulf Beaches 12 (clearwater-beach 3, indian-rocks-beach 3, madeira-beach 2, st-pete-beach 2, treasure-island 1, pass-a-grille 1).
- By kind: museum 24, district 13, gallery 12, market 6, shopping 6, attraction 4, aquarium 3, pier 2, waterfront 2, sports 1, zoo 1, science-center 1, landmark 1, water-park 1.
- Status: 74 open (several with a status_note), 2 seasonal (Saturday Morning Market and Sunday Market St. Pete, both on a September break and back Oct 3 / Oct 4, 2026), 1 temporarily-closed (Woodson African American Museum, roof work from Sep 21, reopening Sep 29, 2026).
- Signature (sparingly): dali-museum, museum-of-fine-arts-st-petersburg, chihuly-collection, st-pete-pier, johns-pass-village, pier-60, clearwater-marine-aquarium, sponge-docks-tarpon-springs, sunshine-skyway-bridge.
- Shared ids created here: dali-museum, museum-of-fine-arts-st-petersburg, st-pete-pier, james-museum, chihuly-collection, imagine-museum, clearwater-marine-aquarium, pier-60, johns-pass-village, sponge-docks-tarpon-springs. Other slices already point at these and at duncan-mcclellan-gallery, florida-craftart, morean-glass-studio, st-petersburg-museum-of-history and zen-glass-studio (exp-land, exp-water, events-spring departs_place/place).

## How candidates were found
1. Visit St. Pete/Clearwater (read with WebFetch; it blocks curl): Things to Do > Museums, Attractions, Arts, Arts & Culture, Shopping, All Museums, Family Activities; the Markets directory (/list/st-pete-clearwater-markets); articles on glass galleries, best places to shop, and art/antiques/collectibles; community pages for St. Petersburg (and its Central Ave, Central Arts, EDGE, Grand Central, Warehouse Arts, Waterfront Museum and Deuces Live district pages), Gulfport, St. Pete Beach, Madeira Beach, Treasure Island, Clearwater Beach, Clearwater, Dunedin, Safety Harbor, Tarpon Springs, Largo and Pinellas Park; and individual listing profiles.
2. Wikipedia: the Pinellas rows of "List of museums in Florida" and the city articles (St. Petersburg, Clearwater, Dunedin, Tarpon Springs, Safety Harbor, Largo, Gulfport, the beach towns), read as raw wikitext.
3. A few WebSearch queries early on (Grand Central, EDGE, Warehouse Arts District, Beach Drive, Imagine Museum, Great Explorations, the Saturday Morning Market). The session-wide WebSearch budget ran out partway through, so later discovery used the tourism listings above and the organizations' own sites.
4. The official site of every candidate (museum, city, county, district association, operator), read with curl (browser user agent, text extracted from the HTML) or with WebFetch where a site blocked curl. Quotes from curl-read pages were string-checked against the saved HTML.

Coordinates: US Census geocoder for street addresses (51), OpenStreetMap/Photon when the OSM feature is the place itself or Census missed (24; e.g. Tarpon Springs Aquarium, where Census matched the wrong side of town), Wikipedia for the Skyway main span (1). Districts use a representative address point, named in each record's notes.

## What was left out, and why
- Other slices' scope: event venues incl. Tropicana Field, Mahaffey, Palladium, Jannus Live, the Coliseum, Ruth Eckerd Hall, Capitol Theatre, Coachman Park/BayCare Sound, Gulfport Casino, Zubrick Magic Theatre (venues-bay); parks, beaches, gardens and preserves incl. Sunken Gardens, Florida Botanical Gardens, Weedon Island, Boyd Hill, Fort De Soto, Honeymoon/Caladesi, the Skyway fishing piers (outdoors); restaurants, bars, breweries, Mazzaro's, Candy Kitchen (eat-pinellas); tours and boat trips, Empower Adventures, mural tours (exp-land / exp-water); pure historic sites: Safford House, Plumb House, St. Nicholas Greek Orthodox Cathedral, Manhattan Casino, Pass-a-Grille Historic District / 8th Avenue, Tarpon Springs Historic District, Tarpon Springs Cultural Center (old City Hall, open only for events) (history-region / venues-bay).
- Not verifiable as open on a page I could read, so not included: Gulf Beaches Historical Museum (site behind a bot check; absent from the VSPC museum list), Merry Pier and Redington Long Pier (no readable status page), Science Center of Pinellas County and Florida Military Aviation Museum (domains do not resolve), National Armed Services & Law Enforcement Memorial Museum (site errors), Haslam's Book Store (its site shows only an old 'closing for a while' notice), Sundial St. Pete (site 503 / TLS error), Ted Williams Museum (inside Tropicana Field), Suntan Art Center and Knot On Main Street (listing addresses inconsistent with their names/locations).
- The Factory St. Pete: its domain now redirects to FloridaRAMA; FloridaRAMA (inside The Factory's Building 5) has a record, the Factory campus does not.
- Low visitor value: Seminole City Center, Largo Mall, Atomic Claw arcade, Largo Central Railroad (monthly rides), individual boutiques.

## Open questions for the verifier
1. Records whose facts rest on a Visit St. Pete/Clearwater page because the official site blocked both curl and WebFetch or gave no details (23): imagine-museum, great-explorations-childrens-museum, central-arts-district, beach-drive, crislip-arcade, gulfport-history-museum, penny-lane-beatles-museum, pier-60, downtown-dunedin, safety-harbor-main-street, leepa-rattner-museum-of-art, cleveland-street-district, corey-avenue, corey-avenue-sunday-market, safety-harbor-market-on-main, dunedin-downtown-market, clay-co-op, bill-jacksons-shop-for-adventure, a-little-room-for-art, studio-1212-art-gallery, st-pete-sunday-market, replay-amusement-museum, celebration-station-clearwater. Their quotes came through WebFetch's extraction and could not be string-checked (also warehouse-arts-district, tyrone-square, countryside-mall, safety-harbor-museum); please re-read them on the source page.
2. Status checks: Pier 60 after the 2024 hurricanes (the city beach page still says 'go fishing on Pier 60'; no Pier 60 status page was found); Leepa-Rattner Museum (official site down); Celebration Station Clearwater (operator site behind a bot check); John's Pass (VSPC says some areas are still recovering).
3. Id collision: gulfport-tuesday-fresh-market is a place here and a series in events-spring. It is the same market; the merge should keep one record (the place, with the series' calendar data) or the events slice should point its place at it.
4. Volatile items to re-check near launch: MFA collection galleries closed Sep 21 to Nov 21, 2026; Woodson Museum reopening Sep 29; Saturday Morning Market back at Al Lang on Oct 3; Clearwater Beach Marina replacement (scheduled to finish Aug 2026; tour boats on new Coronado Drive slips); MAACM garden construction and temporary entrance.
5. Conflicting hours noted in records' notes: Florida CraftArt Second Saturday closing (8 vs 9pm), Palm Harbor Museum (museum site Thu-Sat vs VSPC Wed-Fri; museum site used), Seaside Seabird Sanctuary (9-5 vs 8-4; visit page used), Splash Harbour (5 vs 6pm), DK Farms (ambiguous; left null), Gulfport Tuesday market (2 vs 3pm).
6. sunshine-skyway-bridge is sourced to Wikipedia (no FDOT visitor page was reachable); history-region/timeline may also cover the 1980 disaster. Toll amounts conflict between sources and are omitted.
7. deuces-live, st-petersburg-shuffleboard-club, crislip-arcade, heritage-village and sponge-docks-tarpon-springs have a historic side; if history-region creates records with the same ids, the merge should unite them.


## Verification (2026-09-27)

Adversarial re-check of all 77 records by a second agent. Every record's source_url (and the also_sources behind its claims) was re-opened with WebFetch; where WebFetch or curl hit a bot check (SiteGround captcha, Cloudflare), the page was read through the r.jina.ai reader, and quotes were string-checked with curl where the site allowed it. The session's WebSearch budget was already spent, so closure and news checks used Google News RSS searches (resolved to the publishers' articles and read with WebFetch).

**Result: 79 places** (77 checked, 1 removed, 3 added). 51 records had at least one substantive field corrected; 2 more got a verifier note only; 24 were confirmed unchanged. Regions: St. Petersburg 38, Clearwater & North Pinellas 29, Gulf Beaches 12. Status: 76 open, 2 seasonal (Saturday Morning Market back Oct 3; Kenwood Sunday Market back Oct 4), 1 temporarily closed (Woodson Museum, reopening Sep 29). Records still resting on a Visit St. Pete/Clearwater listing: 16 (down from 23), each re-read and each with a note saying why.

### Fixed (the ones that mattered)
- **penny-lane-beatles-museum**: the VSPC listing was out of date. The museum moved from Dunedin to 146 2nd St N, reopened in August 2026 and now charges $15 (8 and under free), open Wed–Sun 10am–4pm; sources moved to its own site.
- **leepa-rattner-museum-of-art**: confirmed open on its own site (read through the reader); admission is by donation with a suggested $10 (not "free"); hours Tue–Sat 11–5; address 600 E Klosterman Rd; sources moved to the museum.
- **johns-pass-village**: the old status note quoted visitor reviews as if they were the tourism office; rewritten from dated news (Hubbard's boutique reopened Sep 2026; hotel approved Jul 2026). "Pirate ship cruises" removed from the summary (not on the source).
- **pier-60**: post-hurricane status settled: closed nearly a year after Helene/Milton, reopened from the bait house to the T on Sep 1, 2025 (FOX 13, Bay News 9); bait house hours 7am–10pm.
- **museum-of-fine-arts-st-petersburg**: collection galleries close Sep 22 (not 21) to Nov 21, 2026.
- **st-pete-pier**: removed an unsupported "three ADA-compliant trams with four stops" claim; parking and rooftop details re-sourced.
- **Quotes** corrected to the source's exact words: clearwater-beach-marina (was cut mid-sentence), safety-harbor-main-street (was cut at 125 characters), crislip-arcade, corey-avenue-sunday-market, safety-harbor-market-on-main, dunedin-downtown-market and clay-co-op (the old quotes were not on the pages as re-read), tyrone-square.
- **Organizer pages now the source** for dunedin-downtown-market and st-pete-sunday-market (Tampa Bay Markets: Pioneer Park is 420 Main St; the St. Pete market is the "Kenwood Sunday Market St. Pete"), corey-avenue (coreyave.com; "near Blind Pass Road" removed) and clay-co-op.
- **Hours or prices** fixed from the source: dali-museum, imagine-museum, james-museum, florida-holocaust-museum, florida-craftart (Second Saturday until 8pm on both pages now), zen-glass-studio (Sunday hours added), dunedin-history-museum, heritage-village, tarpon-springs-heritage-museum, collection-on-palmetto, dk-farms-and-gardens (hours were readable: Sep/Nov/Dec 10–4, October Mon–Sat 10–7, Sun 10–4), spc-planetarium (fall 2026 Wednesday shows at 7pm), smugglers-cove (holiday hours, phone), splash-harbour-water-park, replay-amusement-museum (adults $16, kids $10), safety-harbor-art-and-music-center (boutique hours), marlene-rose-gallery (phone).

### Removed
- **a-little-room-for-art**: could not confirm it is open. Its domain now serves an unrelated article site, the VSPC listing is the only page naming it, and no 2025–2026 page or news shows it operating after the 2024 hurricanes flooded Pass-a-Grille. No other slice referenced it.

All 58 street addresses re-geocoded with the Census geocoder and compared with the stored points. 40 match exactly; the rest are OpenStreetMap features within 30–380 m of the address point, except tarpon-springs-aquarium (Census matched S Pinellas Ave, 4.3 km off; the stored OSM aquarium feature at 1722 N Pinellas Ave is right) and leepa-rattner-museum-of-art (Census interpolated along Klosterman Rd, 1.35 km off; the stored OSM museum feature on the SPC campus is right).
